summary.headline: IOL Chemicals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR756 crore and PAT 90% to INR64.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.6%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR756 crore against INR551 crore a year earlier, up 37%. EBITDA rose 60.7% to INR111 crore, lifting margin to 14.6% from 12.4%, and PAT grew 89.9% to INR64.5 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher capacity utilisation, product mix, export realisations and operational efficiencies, and said there was no material inventory gain in the quarter. FY27 guidance was retained at 15-20% revenue growth, 14-15% EBITDA margin and 25-30% exports, with management saying revenue could exceed the INR2,600-2,700 crore range but not upgrading guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs 36% in Q1 FY26; non-ibu revenue up 67% YoY
Management did not split volume vs price

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals (API)
segments.commentary: Non-ibuprofen products were 43% of pharma revenue, up 67% YoY; growth described as broad-based across the portfolio. Most assets run at 80-95% utilisation, with paracetamol lower at about 55% of enhanced 10,800 MTPA capacity.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Management said the chemical segment margin trended up in the quarter, helped by higher ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride capacity, better realisations and higher exports. Triacetin plant (6,000 MTPA) started production only in May 2026, with steady-state revenue potential of about INR120 crore a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27: revenue growth of 15-20% (management said around 20% in Q&A), EBITDA margin 14-15%, exports about 25-30% of revenue.
Management said the INR2,600-2,700 crore full-year revenue guidance remains unchanged, may be crossed in the current scenario, but will not be upgraded.
FY28 (indicative, conditional on current scenario): revenue growth 15-20% and EBITDA margin 15-17%.
Near term: non-ibuprofen to reach about 50% of pharma revenue, with roughly 50% ibuprofen; by FY29, non-ibu expected at 50-55% of API segment with margins similar to ibuprofen.
Capex of about INR200 crore a year; about 60% expansion and new products, 40% infrastructure and efficiency. Next major project on the 101-acre land is not expected in FY27.
Regulatory: two to three more quarters expected for Triacetin approvals.
capex_capacity: Paracetamol capacity tripled from 3,600 MTPA to 10,800 MTPA; operating at about 55%, targeted near 70% by end FY27.
Triacetin plant of 6,000 MTPA commenced production in May 2026; capacity to ramp as market penetration grows. Inputs are acetic acid and glycerol.
Capacity of ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride increased during the period.
Capex of around INR200 crore per year, with INR100-200 crore spent annually over the last four to five years.
R&D spend of INR26 crore in FY26; analytical equipment bought (XRD, LCMS, GCMS).
101-acre land parcel held for future expansion; statutory permissions in process; no project expected to commission in FY27.
demand_pricing: Healthy demand across paracetamol, pantoprazole, metformin, fenofibrate, clopidogrel and levetiracetam. Management said price increases were passed on to customers.

Ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride prices rose sharply in March 2026 after the US-Iran conflict; since then prices have been stable to slightly easing, and management expects the raw-material-to-ethyl-acetate spread to hold.
Energy and logistics costs rose in the quarter; management said most of the increase was passed on.
Sequential gross margin fell as input costs rose before finished-product prices fully caught up. Some prices were pre-agreed with large customers.
Exports: some export customers have agreed quantities, so the export share can move quarter to quarter.

Regulatory: CEP approval for all products; US FDA approval for five products, with two to three more pending ANDA approval by formulators; NMPA China approval for clopidogrel; ibuprofen previously approved in China.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for paracetamol given weak demand in past years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity was tripled to 10,800 MTPA, utilisation is about 55%, and it expects about 70% by year-end. Demand is growing, with domestic traction and exports.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 profit came from one-time inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no material inventory gain this quarter; a 10-15 day benefit existed at the end of Q4 FY26. The improvement was attributed to utilisation, mix, efficiencies and export realisations.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA outperformance came from operating leverage versus mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin gain mainly to internal efficiencies and higher utilisation, with no major product mix change apart from greater export penetration.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a split of pharma growth between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a numerical split. It said the majority came from higher volumes, with higher export realisations also contributing, and most assets at 80-95% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth muted in prior quarters and how long will demand last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher volumes, better pricing on established products and new products, and cost pass-through. It said there is reasonable order-book visibility for the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Triacetin revenue potential and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Production started only after May 2026, so about one month was in Q1. Steady-state revenue potential is about INR120 crore a year from the 6,000 MTPA plant. Management declined to compare its margin with ethyl acetate.

risks_watch: Raw material and energy price volatility (linked to the US-Iran conflict); margin sensitivity to lag in passing through costs.
Export share (28.5% in Q1) may fall back toward the 25-30% guidance band if customer agreed quantities shift.
Paracetamol utilisation at about 55% against the target of 70% by year-end.
Pending US FDA approvals for two to three ANDA-linked products and Triacetin regulatory approvals expected in two to three quarters.
FY28 margin outlook is explicitly conditional on the current scenario; management said it may not hold if conditions change within six months.
Lack of disclosure on the volume versus price split and on the regulated versus non-regulated export mix.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the diversification story, but guarded on forward numbers: management held guidance, declined to upgrade it, and said FY28 targets depend on current conditions. It was evasive on the pharma volume/price split, the R&D pipeline, CMO opportunities and the regulated-market export mix.
key_quotes: We have started FY27 on a strong note, with healthy demand across key products, improved capacity utilization, favorable product mix, and continued focus on operational efficiency.
Our objective is not merely to add capacities, but to build meaningful and sustainable positions across a diversified API portfolio.
So the guidance will be remaining in the same line. However, we will be able to -- having the current scenario, we think that we may cross that number. But we don't want to upgrade the guidance
Abhay Raj Singh: Maulik ji, this is on the basis of the current scenario. Suppose down the line in next six-month scenario got changed, then what we are saying may not be possible.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% (held, ~20% in Q&A) with 14-15% EBITDA margin; backed by Q1 revenue +37%, 80-95% utilisation in most pharma assets, and recently commissioned paracetamol and Triacetin capacity, but no specific new order book or large capacity timed for FY27 beyond ramp-ups.
